Plot local-projection results

Source: R/lp-plot.R
autoplot.lpm.Rd

autoplot() returns a ggplot; plot() prints it and returns it invisibly. Shaded ribbons are the stored band levels (widest lightest).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lpm'
autoplot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lp_state'
autoplot(object, type = c("states", "diff"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'lp_smooth'
autoplot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lp_supt'
autoplot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lp_forecast'
autoplot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lpm'
plot(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lp_state'
plot(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lp_supt'
plot(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lp_forecast'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

object, x

a result of lp(), lp_state(), lp_smooth(), lp_panel(), lp_joint(), lp_supt() or lp_forecast().

...

unused (plot() passes them to autoplot()).

type

lp_state only: "states" or "diff".

Value

a ggplot object.

Details

  • lpm, lp_joint, lp_panel: response paths, one panel per response.

  • lp_state: the high and low state overlaid (type = "states") or their difference (type = "diff").

  • lp_smooth: smoothed against raw local projection.

  • lp_supt: pointwise against sup-t simultaneous bands.

  • lp_forecast: direct forecast fan chart.

See also

Other local projections: compare_lp_var(), lp(), lp_forecast(), lp_joint(), lp_panel(), lp_smooth(), lp_state(), lp_supt(), tidy.lpm()

Examples

fit <- lp(yraw, shock = rate, horizon = 8, lags = 2, contemp = c(infl, unemp))
autoplot(fit)
